title: AI model vs agent harness vs orchestration layer
description: Most people throwing around the word "agent" have no idea what's actually happening under the hood. A model just predicts the next token. A harness wraps that in a loop and hands it tools to act on the world. An orchestration layer runs dozens of those harnesses in parallel without blowing past the context window. Understanding all three is going to be one of the most valuable skills as agents start replacing real knowledge work. I break down exactly how it fits together inside my community. Link in bio.
transcript: What's the difference between an AI model, an AI agent harness, and an agent orchestration layer? An AI model, put simply, is a neural network that has inputs and outputs, and its goal is to just predict the next token in a sentence that you give it. When people talk about an AI agent, all it really is is putting that input-output cycle of an AI model into a loop that does that multiple times, looping over a certain task or goal. AI agent harnesses also introduce the idea of tools, which allow an AI model to actually interact with the external world. And the way that this works is that the AI model has been trained that it can actually take actions on the external world if it outputs a little block of text that says, "I want to use this tool." Then the agentic coding harness, which interprets all that text output by the model, senses that little block of text that the AI model generated saying, "I want to use this tool." And the harness, which is made of traditional code, interprets that text and actually executes a script to call that tool. The internal loop of an AI agent harness can get extremely complicated. There's a lot of different nuances involved, and as you can see, all the top model companies are working really hard to create the best, most efficient agentic coding harness. Agent orchestration is when you get into the world of using multiple coding harnesses in parallel at the same time, or working for really long periods, or working within the same kind of context domain for a really long time, like within a business. AI models have a limited context window, and this limitation also transfers over to agentic coding harnesses, so you can only fit so much information in the AI's brain at once. And a big part of agentic orchestration is understanding how to organize that external information so that you can package up just the right amount of information to make it into one context window to have your agents actually do productive work. This involves task management systems where you delegate tasks to different agents, having a shared knowledge base that stores a really large swath of memory that can be packaged up to send to specific agents when they need it. Understanding the technicals of how AI models generate their responses, how those responses are interpreted and acted upon by agentic coding harnesses, and then how those harnesses can be organized into orchestration layers that orchestrate many agents at once can be some of the most valuable skills in a future where agentic coding harnesses are starting to replace real knowledge work in real businesses. If you're interested in getting nerdy, diving deep into these types of topics, how agentic coding harnesses work, and how to orchestrate them into real business automation systems, that is all we talk about in my school community, and I have plug-and-play systems to get you started, all hosted in there. The link is in my bio, and I'd love to see you there and get learning.
